issues.issue: "[E]ffective as of the date first above written" conflicts with the preamble's statement that the Agreement "shall be effective as hereinafter provided." One fixes April 12, 1996; the other defers effectiveness to some unidentified later provision.

The exclusion is of the portions of the two fee tracts "lying in a 2,000' radius circle sorrounding Well KF-1053," while Section 2(D) describes the same circle as "centered around" the well and the recital as "surrounding" it. Whether the well is the center and how the arc is surveyed on the ground is not fixed by any of the three.

Exhibit "C" imposes every geological duty on "Operator," a term the Agreement never defines and which need not be Farmee, yet Section 3(D)(1) conditions Farmee's earning on compliance with these requirements. Whether Farmee is answerable for a third-party operator's failures is unresolved.

The samples are to be deposited with the proviso that "EREX will have free access thereto," but "EREX" is nowhere defined or identified as Equitable Resources Energy Company in the Agreement. "[Q]ualified wellsite geologist" and "thoroughly and timely" are likewise given no standard.

"Significant indications of reservoir quality porosity" must be "adequately tested in accordance with good oilfield practices," three undefined standards stacked on each other. Whether a given show required testing is not answerable from the text.

"Routine daily prepaid report" is garbled — "prepaid" does not fit a report — and the clause requires a daily report "Monday through Friday" while also being "confirmed daily in writing," leaving weekends unaddressed. What is actually owed on non-drilling days is unclear.

"Non-routine occurrences such as notification of significant shows, intent to core, test or log" is an open-ended catch-all introduced by "such as," so the enumerated items do not bound the duty. What else counts as non-routine, reportable "immediately," is left to argument.

The duty attaches to reports "when received by the Operator," which does not address reports the Operator itself prepares and never receives from anyone. "[A]ll reports, charts, logs, analyses, surveys and forms pertaining to the subject well" is also unbounded in time.

The list of required well surveys is a check-box list whose marks are indeterminate — a stray "i" beside Density, a blank rule beside Neutron, and an unfilled "Other" — so which logs are actually required cannot be read off the page. Section 3(D)(1) makes earning depend on compliance with these requirements.

"Timely notice of intent to core, test or log" sets no number of hours or days and is measured only by the purpose that Farmor's representative "may be present to witness same." Whether short notice was timely is left entirely at large.

The introduction requires "one copy of the following (unless otherwise specified)," item (a) then requires "Two final prints," and a heading "THREE COPIES" precedes items (b)–(e), so the number of copies owed is internally inconsistent. The catch-all "[a]ny other data pertinent to the drilling, testing and surveying" has no boundary either.

"[F]ull information on the completion progress" is an open-ended standard that the itemized list "including one copy of the data listed below" expressly does not limit. What else "full information" requires is undefined.

Exhibit "C" directs all reports and data to Farmor's office "Attn: Mike Stamper," while Section 10(B) directs all notices and correspondence to "ATTN: Lester Zitkus" at a differently stated address. Which delivery satisfies the notice and well-information obligations is unresolved.

The granting language leaves the size of the circle blank and grants the right to "operate, maintain and rework" the well, whereas Section 2(D) fixes 80-acre circles for gas wells and 40-acre circles for oil wells and speaks of the right to "operate, maintain and produce." The form and the earning definition do not describe the same estate.

The assignment lasts "so long as oil and gas ... is produced in paying quantities" or the well is shut in, with no temporary-cessation savings clause and no definition of paying quantities. Whether a period of non-production terminates the assigned operating rights is left open.

The assignment is made "without any warranty whatsoever" and disclaims all title warranties, yet the next paragraph assigns "any and all rights and privileges possessed by" Assignor under its deeds and leases. Whether that grant carries any implied assurance of what Assignor in fact possesses is contestable.

The indemnity covers claims "incident to, or arising directly or indirectly from, operations by Assignee" with no express mention of Assignor's own negligence or fault. It also overlaps Section 8(A) of the Farmout Agreement without saying which governs post-assignment operations.

The rights assigned are those "necessary or convenient" for operation, maintenance, reworking and production, a standard with no boundary — "convenient" in particular could reach far beyond the well. The grant is then made "expressly subject to" the underlying leases without identifying them.

The form reserves an overriding royalty at a blank rate on a blank substance and contains no escalation mechanism, while Section 4 fixes 12.50% of 8/8 with reserved rights to escalate to 16% and 18.75% (and 1.5%/3.5%/6.5% for burdened oil) on Payout. The executed assignment and Section 4 cannot both state the royalty regime.

"[G]rants, conveys and assigns other such rights to Assignee only to the extent set forth herein" is garbled — "other such rights" has no antecedent — while the same sentence reserves title to "the aforementioned lands, and all rights connected thereto." What passes to Assignee is left to inference.

This paragraph permits Assignee to assign on written notice provided it retains at least a 25% working interest, while Section 15(D) of the Farmout Agreement forbids any assignment by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent. The two consent regimes are irreconcilable on their face.

The reservation of all strata "extending below the ___ formation" leaves the formation name blank, so the vertical limit of the grant is measured by nothing, while Section 3(E) measures depths earned as 100' below total depth drilled and not more than 4,000'. Which limit controls the assigned depths cannot be determined.

The assignment is made binding on and for the benefit of "their respective successors and assigns," which is in tension with the restriction in the same instrument (and Section 15(D)) barring assignment without Assignor's consent. Whether a non-consented successor takes the benefit is unaddressed.

The assignment is made "subject to the terms and conditions of that certain unrecorded Farmout Agreement," so the recorded conveyance's extent depends on an unrecorded instrument, and Section 17 says the Farmout's covenants "run with said Farmout Lands." How the Farmout's terms bind third parties or survive its Section 13 termination is left open.
